text:
sara: Heads-up — since ~02:00 UTC yesterday we've had p95/p99 regressions on tool-router routes. Multiple customer tickets (timeouts / 504s). Posting notes and a quick repro.

ops-bot: [ALERT] metric=tool-router.latency.p99 value=5.6s cluster=prod-us-west-2 window=15m

maya: Ugh. Any single request id we can look at?

sara: One customer request id: req_20260317_9f8c. Attached router trace shows long wait in schema validation step (~3.2s). Sample payload below.

sara: ```
POST /v1/router/call HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-psi",
  "input": "summarize the invoice and extract line items",
  "tools": ["invoice_parser"],
  "tool_schema": { /* big JSON schema, ~120kb */ }
}
Response timings: total=5.4s, router_validation=3.2s, route_lookup=0.3s, send_to_model=1.0s
```

kevin: Thanks. Looks like JSON Schema validation is dominating when tool_schema is large. We've seen this with schema-heavy tool calls before. Is it only with the big schemas or all tool calls?

sara: Mostly the large ones. Small schemas still fine. Customer load spikes amplify it so p95 moves up.

anjali: Customer impacted: AcmePayments (support#3452). They reported several 30s client timeouts, devs say they hit retries which made load worse.

kevin: Quick mitigation options:
- disable router-side schema validation for canary customers (config flag)
- increase thread pool for validation workers (short-term)
- async validation: accept request, hand off schema check to background/eval and fail-safe run tools without validation if validation not complete (temporary)
- stream results earlier to reduce client timeouts

maya: Can we patch a config toggle now? Where's the flag?

kevin: There's an env flag: TOOL_ROUTER_SCHEMA_VALIDATION (true by default). I can flip for a small canary (10% traffic) to test.

sara: Please do canary + note which customers are in the bucket. Also add an annotation so we can revert if false-positive issues happen.

kevin: Rolling canary: set TOOL_ROUTER_SCHEMA_VALIDATION=false for router-pool-canary-3. Will monitor.

ops-bot: [DEPLOY] rollout start cluster=prod-us-west-2 pool=router-pool-canary-3 user=kevin ts=2465000027

kevin: Canary results after 7m: p50 240ms -> 220ms, p95 1.8s -> 640ms, p99 5.3s -> 920ms. Looks promising.

maya: Nice. Any errors from tool misuse after disabling validation?

kevin: So far no tool errors. We did see a slight uptick in malformed-tool warnings in logs (10 over 7m) but none caused downstream failures. Logging increased for rejected tool calls that would have been blocked.

anjali: I'll message AcmePayments and tell them we rolled a safe canary change and ask them to verify. Also add to their ticket.

sara: Next steps:
- if canary stable for 30m, rollout to 50% then full.
- engineering: follow-up task to move heavy validation to async path or offload to a validation service (ticket ENG-ff-472).
- product: evaluate exposing client-side validation helpers (so schema checked before hitting router)

kevin: Quick reproduction steps for infra folks:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/router/call -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d @payload.json
2) payload.json should include a ~100kb tool_schema object (use repeated nested pattern)
3) measure X-Request-Id / X-Router-Latency header

sara: Logs snippet for req_20260317_9f8c: ```
[router] req=req_20260317_9f8c stage=validation dur=3240ms
[router] req=req_20260317_9f8c stage=dispatch dur=1020ms
[router] req=req_20260317_9f8c status=200 total=5460ms
```

kevin: Created a short-lived monitor dashboard and an alert to auto-scale validation workers if p95 > 1s for 5m. Also added a manual rollback runbook.

ops-bot: [ALERT RESOLVED] tool-router.p99 back to 920ms (canary).

maya: Can we add a lint/SDK helper so customers get schema warnings earlier? That will reduce bad payloads.

anjali: Adding as product request. I'll link to AcmePayments ticket so we can include them in beta.

sara: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread updated. If anyone finds a request that still hits >3s validation, paste req id here. :thumbsup:
